evidence: createApp registers Express routes that only parse requests, call services.users/projects/tasks methods, and write HTTP responses: this is transport work.
bodyOf/requiredString/optionalString/optionalDate/singleQueryValue check only the type and format of request input, which is normal adapter work.
parseStatus uses isTaskStatus and TASK_STATUSES from the domain to check status values instead of defining its own list of valid statuses.
taskToJson converts a Task into a JSON response object (ISO dates, nulls), which is presentation and transport work.
The error middleware maps ValidationError/NotFoundError/ConflictError/SyntaxError to HTTP status codes 422/404/409/400/500, which is transport-specific translation.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts is an HTTP transport adapter built on Express, and everything in it fits the infrastructure layer. Its work falls into four groups. First, it parses and checks the shape of incoming requests (bodyOf, requiredString, optionalString, optionalDate, singleQueryValue). Second, it turns request data into calls to the application services (users, projects, tasks). Third, it serializes domain entities into JSON responses (taskToJson). Fourth, it maps domain error types to HTTP status codes in the error middleware. None of the business decisions happen here. Assignment, completion, conflict detection and the list of valid statuses are left to the application services or the domain: parseStatus calls the domain's isTaskStatus and TASK_STATUSES instead of defining its own. The fallback of description to "" is a default applied to the input, not a business rule. The checks reject malformed input, such as wrong types, empty strings and invalid ISO dates, and do not enforce domain invariants. The file has no persistence logic and no domain policy.
